items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: I've heard some of his recordings and my God, I just think they're terrific.

ctx.x: Who do you like or do you have any taste for the modern jazz pianists of today? Do you find any kinship with them in particular?

Oh, definitely Charlie, definitely. I follow the pianists, I guess, practically all of them. I've lost track of some of the modern ones because they're coming so fast these days that I just can hardly keep up with them. But I've kept up with most of them and I just think that they're just the greatest. Like for instance, I think George Shearing is superb. I think Amma Jamal is. I think Errol Garner in his own way. I mean a lot of people just don't particularly care for him, but I think he's real great. And, well,…

That's kind of brings us into my next point very naturally. You're known internationally, basically, as a ragtime pianist. Do you think that this is an apt description of your style? I'm sure it limits your range to call you a ragtime pianist. What do you think of the tag personally, though?
